title: 第14章 瓦丁村的傻姑娘第15章 塞娜
slug: 百世轮回词条无限累加
lines: 瓦丁村的夜并不安静。
村东头的狗在那儿瞎叫唤，也不知道是看见了耗子还是怎么地。
隔壁老汤姆家的那头毛驴也跟着起哄，昂昂昂地叫个不停，听着像是在拉风箱。
塞娜趴在阁楼的小窗户上，手里攥着一块硬邦邦的黑面包干，也没吃，就那么用大拇指摩挲着上面粗糙的纹路。
她是铁匠老巴克的闺女。今年十六。
在这个年纪的姑娘，要么已经嫁人去给别人生娃煮饭，要么就在盘算着该嫁给村里那个杀猪的还是那个种地的。
但塞娜不一样。
她不想嫁给杀猪的，那人身上总是一股子猪大肠味儿，洗都洗不掉。
她也不想嫁给种地的，一辈子脸朝黄土背朝天，过得跟她爹老巴克一样，成天就围着个火炉子转。
她想嫁个……不一样的。
哪怕是那个只会吹牛皮的瘸腿吟游诗人，也比这帮满脑子只有麦子和猪肉的糙汉子强。
至少人家嘴里能蹦出几个好听的词儿，知道外面的世界有个叫“大海”的大水坑，知道城里的贵族老爷们是用银子做的勺子吃饭。
可惜，她长得不行。
塞娜下意识地摸了摸自己的脸。那里有些坑坑洼洼的，那是小时候出天花留下的麻子。
虽然不多，但在那帮挑剔的小伙子眼里，这就成了掉价的理由。
塞娜叹了气。
就在她准备关上窗户，钻进那条散发着霉味儿的被窝里睡觉时，眼神却突然定住了。
今晚月亮挺大。
像个白森森的盘子挂在天上，照得地上一片惨白。
村口那棵不知道活了多少年的老树底下，多了个东西。
确切地说，是个人。
那人蜷缩在树根的大坑里，身子缩成一团，跟只被雨淋湿了的鹌鹑似的。身上盖着的一层落叶，随着呼吸一上一下地起伏。
“那是谁？”
塞娜心里咯噔一下。
这村子偏得连收税官都懒得来，平时除了老皮特那辆破马车，也就是几只野狗会在村口晃悠。
流浪汉？
逃兵？
还是……传说中那种受了伤、不得不躲到乡下来养伤的落魄骑士？
最后那个念头刚一冒出来，就像野草一样在塞娜心里疯长。
你看那故事书里不都这么写吗？
某个月黑风高的晚上，单纯善良的农家女救了一个满身是血的英俊男人。
男人为了报恩，带她回了城堡，从此过上了顿顿吃白面包、天天穿丝绸裙子的好日子。
虽然理智告诉她，那大概率就是个偷鸡摸狗的贼，或者是个满身虱子的乞丐。
但那种叫“万一呢”的念头，挠得她心痒痒。
“我就看一眼。”
塞娜在心里跟自己说。
“就一眼。如果是乞丐，我就回来睡觉。如果是贼，反正也不远，我就喊老爹拿锤子砸他。”
她轻手轻脚地离开窗边，没敢点灯。摸黑穿上那双稍微体面点的旧皮鞋，披上一件打着补丁的粗布外套。
老巴克在前屋睡得跟死猪一样，呼噜声震得房梁都在抖。
塞娜像只猫一样溜出了后门。
外面的风有点硬，吹在脸上生疼。
塞娜裹紧了衣裳，一步一步往村口挪。
每走一步，心跳就快一分。咚咚咚的，像是要从嗓子眼蹦出来。
越靠近那棵老树，那股子混合着泥土和陌生气息的味道就越重。
content_en:
The night in Wading Village was not quiet.
The dog at the east end of the village was barking blindly. I don't know if it saw a mouse or something.
The donkey from Old Tom's house next door also started braying loudly, sounding like a bellows.
Senna was lying on the small attic window, holding a hard piece of black bread in her hand. She didn't eat it, just rubbing the rough lines on it with her thumb.
She is the daughter of old blacksmith Buck. This year is sixteen.
Girls at this age have either already married to give birth to children and cook for others, or they are deciding whether to marry the pig-killer or the farmer in the village.
But Senna is different.
She didn't want to marry a pig butcher. He always smelled like pig intestines and couldn't be washed away.
She also didn't want to marry a farmer and spend her whole life with her face turned to the earth and her back turned to the sky, living like her father, Old Buck, who stayed around the stove all day long.
She wanted to marry someone...different.
Even the lame bard who only knows how to brag is better than these rough guys who only think about wheat and pork.
At least he can have a few nice words coming out of his mouth, he knows that there is a big puddle called "the sea" in the outside world, and he knows that the noble men in the city eat with spoons made of silver.
It's a pity that she doesn't look good.
Sena subconsciously touched her face. There are some potholes there, which are the pockmarks left by smallpox when I was a child.
Although it wasn't much, in the eyes of those picky young men, this became a reason to drop the price.
"Alas."
Senna sighed.
Just when she was about to close the window and get into the musty-smelling bed to sleep, her eyes suddenly froze.
The moon is quite big tonight.
Like a white plate hanging in the sky, it illuminated the ground palely.
There was something extra under the old tree at the entrance of the village that had lived for who knows how many years.
Rather, a person.
The man huddled in the big hole at the root of the tree, huddled up like a quail soaked by the rain. The layer of fallen leaves covering her body rises and falls with her breathing.
"Who is that?"
Sena's heart skipped a beat.
This village is so lazy that even the tax collector doesn't bother to come. Usually, except for Old Pete's broken carriage, a few wild dogs wander around the entrance to the village.
tramp?
deserter?
Or... the legendary down-and-out knight who was injured and had to hide in the countryside to recuperate?
As soon as the last thought came up, it grew like a weed in Sena's heart.
You see, isn’t that what the storybooks say?
One dark and stormy night, a simple and kind-hearted peasant girl saved a handsome man covered in blood.
In order to repay his kindness, the man took her back to the castle, and from then on she lived a good life of eating white bread every meal and wearing silk skirts every day.
Although her reason told her that he was most likely a thief or a beggar covered in lice.
But the thought of "what if" tickled her heart.
"I'll just take a look."
Sena said to herself in her mind.
"Just one look. If it's a beggar, I'll come back and sleep. If it's a thief, it's not far anyway, so I'll tell dad to hit him with a hammer."
She quietly left the window, not daring to light the lamp. In the dark, he put on his somewhat decent old leather shoes and put on a patched coarse cloth coat.
Old Buck slept like a dead pig in the front room, his snoring making the rafters shake.
Senna slipped out the back door like a cat.
The wind outside was a bit strong and it hurt my face.
Sena wrapped her clothes tightly and moved towards the village entrance step by step.
Every time I take a step, my heart beats faster. There was a thumping sound, as if it was about to pop out of the throat.
The closer I got to the old tree, the stronger the smell of earth and strangeness became.
